availability_evidence: Annual report pages 83 and 84 state that the financial statements were authorised for issue by the Board on 9 April 2020; the exact Companies House filing bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue was broadly flat at £80.86m, while operating profit before the exceptional item fell 21% to £9.10m and underlying PBT fell 19% to £8.76m; gross margin eased 43bps to 35.4%. Polyolefin Foams revenue fell 10%, partly offset by 20% HPP growth. Net debt rose to £31.90m from £12.96m and leverage to 2.0x from 0.7x as the major capacity programme continued, though operating cash inflow improved and £17.7m of the facility remained undrawn. H2 cost management and reduced variable pay were already reflected, while the Board identified Covid-19 uncertainty but considered liquidity sufficient.
already_announced_exclusion: The H2 cost management and reduced variable-pay actions, capacity-investment programme, bank covenant amendment and liquidity measures disclosed before report approval are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Material underlying profit deterioration and sharply higher leverage support elevated pressure, but broadly stable revenue, HPP growth, positive operating cash flow, covenant headroom and available liquidity provide substantial contrary evidence.

availability_evidence: Annual report pages 111 and 112 state that the financial statements were authorised for issue by the Board on 6 April 2022; the exact Companies House filing bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue rose 22% to £100.8m, but severe production-input, freight and overhead inflation reduced gross margin by 720bps to 26.4%. Operating profit fell 11% to £8.1m, PBT fell 16% to £7.0m and EPS fell 39%. Net debt improved modestly to £34.3m from £35.6m, leverage held at 2.1x and operating activities generated £10.9m before £7.0m capital expenditure and £3.1m dividends. Management described the year as mixed and had already implemented pricing responses, commissioned Poland capacity and pursued operational measures to address input and logistics pressure.
already_announced_exclusion: The sales-price responses, Poland facility commissioning and ramp-up, capacity investments, supply-chain mitigation and operational actions disclosed before report approval are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Exceptional revenue growth and stable debt metrics provide strong contrary evidence, but severe margin compression and declines in operating profit, PBT and EPS support elevated pressure, especially on margins.

availability_evidence: Annual report pages 115 and 116 state that the financial statements were authorised for issue by the Board on 5 April 2024; the exact Companies House filing bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Group revenue was broadly flat at £127.0m, while gross margin improved 190bps to 32.3%, operating profit rose 9% to £15.1m and PBT rose 5% to a record £12.8m. The core foams businesses increased operating profit 23% and margin 280bps, although MEL losses increased as ReZorce investment continued and EPS fell 8% because of tax. Net debt rose 13% to £31.6m, but leverage remained 1.2x and the balance sheet was described as strong. Management expected further growth and made continued ReZorce investment contingent on progress and expected outcomes.
already_announced_exclusion: The ReZorce investment programme and its contingent funding approach, prior pricing and margin-recovery actions, and capacity and efficiency initiatives disclosed before report approval are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Record PBT, higher operating profit, material margin recovery, strong core-foams performance and stable low leverage provide very strong contrary evidence. Flat revenue, higher net debt and growing MEL losses create only limited residual pressure.
